So in fact the government's main intention in submitting this amendment to the Foreign Exchange Act is to stop the dollar's price from rising in the Maldives even today, and to work in every way possible to reduce the price at which dollars can be bought in the dollar market. What a government working properly with good intentions must do is work with good intentions. The people will see that this is work done with good intentions. Neither because of this, nor because of these amendments brought to this bill, is it designed to benefit a particular individual or a particular person. The government now: the MMA said even yesterday that it will increase the percentage of dollars released to banks. Because of that too, relief will come for making TTs and for businesses. Because of that relief, food prices will fall. So when all these things are connected, as I believe, this black market for dollars will also change and will also come down. Then we need to consider important points in this. What has been invested in the Maldives, resorts and tourism-sector investors have invested by taking very large loans and so on. In the Maldives, especially, very many businesspeople have taken very big risks. For example, if we look at the war still going on in the Middle East, Honourable Speaker, even if the transport system of only one country among them is affected or changed, a great many bookings are being cancelled at the Maldives' tourist resorts, guesthouses and other places where tourists come. So because of that too very big changes are coming. Flight tickets have become extremely expensive. The rise in the price of the dollar, food and everything in the country's economy are all connected to all these changes. Even in all these circumstances, we should thank this government of ours, because, and I do not mean any particular government, the many millions borrowed by past governments in the name of the development of this country and so on, one billion dollars, were repaid not even two months ago. One billion dollars. This is not, the way the MDP certainly printed money,

something that can be printed, the dollar. Then some members said that to repay the dollar loan, a bit was taken from one place, a bit from here, a bit from another place, and like this from another company. Isn't that fortunate? Previously, large loans of this kind taken by the Maldivian state were repaid by taking another loan to repay that loan. However, without taking another loan, two months ago our government repaid one billion dollars' worth of loans without borrowing money from anywhere else. At that time, these large investments in the Maldives were mortgaged. Dharumavantha Hospital was under mortgage. Large schools in the Maldives were under mortgage. Many places like this came to be mortgaged. So, if we look at the world stage at this moment, if a large loan owed like this could not be repaid, this country could be entirely ruined, become bankrupt, and the people could end up destitute. We will have seen the situation our neighbour Sri Lanka faced recently. Because the government could not repay a debt it had to repay. They still cannot recover, Honourable Speaker. The people had to stay in darkness without food or drink. So it was this government that saved this country from going into that situation. If the MDP had returned to power in 2013, 2023, I do not know what situation this country would be in today. They are very good at talking about the economy. When they left after completing 5 years, in this Maldives, [unclear] in the 5 years of the last MDP administration, 10 resorts had opened. 10 resorts in 5 years. That is true; budgets of 40 billion, 50 billion were passed in this place. I do not know what happened to those budgets, Honourable Speaker. So there is no point talking politics on a bill like this. What I will say is that these are bills this government submits with good intentions and a noble purpose. I am very happy that a member of our MDA, the Honourable Member for Velidhoo constituency, Mohamed Abbas... Mohamed Abbas is a sharp-minded person. Having looked at and studied this bill properly, he spoke saying that this is a good bill. They have been submitted as good amendments. So, thanking everyone very much, I conclude my remarks by asking the MDP members not to speak further against this bill and to shorten this debate today. Thank you very much, Speaker.

speeches.name: Abdul Raheem Abdulla
speeches.heading: ރިޔާސަތުން ވާހަކަދެއްކެވުން:
speeches.dv: އާދެ! ޝުކުރިއްޔާ އިއްޒަތްތެރި މެންބަރު. މިހާރު ފުރުޞަތު މި އަރުވަނީ ގަލޮޅު ދެކުނު ދާއިރާގެ އިއްޒަތްތެރި މެންބަރު މީކާއީލު އަޙްމަދު ނަސީމަށް.
speeches.en: Yes! Thank you, Honourable Member. I now give the floor to the Honourable Member for Galolhu South constituency, Meekail Ahmed Nasym.

speeches.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
speeches.heading: ގަލޮޅު ދެކުނު ދާއިރާގެ މެންބަރު މީކާއީލު އަޙްމަދު ނަސީމް ވާހަކަދެއްކެވުން:
speeches.dv:
ޝުކުރިއްޔާ އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް. ބޭރު ފައިސާއާ ބެހޭ ގާނޫނަށް ސަރުކާރުން އަނެއްކާ ވެސް ހުށަހަޅުއްވާފައިވާ އިޞްލާޙާ އެކު؛ އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް، މި އިޞްލާޙަކީ ޙަޤީޤަތުގައި ސަރުކާރު ފެއިލްވެއްޖެކަމުގެ އިޢުތިރާފެއް. މި އިޞްލާޙަކީ ސަރުކާރުގެ ފިސްކަލް ޕޮލިސީ ފެއިލްވެއްޖެކަމުގެ އިޢުތިރާފެއް. އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް؛ މާލީ ހާލަތު ސަރުކާރަށް ނޭނގި މިހާތަނަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ އިޤްތިޞާދާ އެކު ރައީސް މުޢިއްޒު ކުރައްވަމުންދިޔަ އެކްސްޕެރިމެންޓް އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް، ފެއިލްވެއްޖެކަމުގެ އިޢުތިރާފު. އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް؛ މީގެ 2 އަހަރެއްހާ ދުވަސް ކުރިން ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ އިޤްތިޞާދީ ވަޒީރު ވަރަށް ފާޅުކަން ބޮޑު ގޮތެއްގައި ވިދާޅުވީ ޕީ.އެން.ސީއަށް، ސަރުކާރަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ރައްޔިތުންގެ މަޖިލީހުގެ ސުޕަރ މެޖޯރިޓީ ލިބިއްޖެ ނަމަ ޑޮލަރުގެ އަގު ތިރިވާނެއޭ. އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް؛ އޭގެ ދެ އަހަރު ފަހުން، އޭރު 18 ރުފިޔާއަށް ލިބެމުން އައި ޑޮލަރު މިއަދު 22 ރުފިޔާއަށް ވެސް ނުލިބޭ. އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް؛ ވަރަށް ފަޚުރުވެރިކަމާ އެކު އެބަ ވިދާޅުވޭ ޑޮލަރަކަށް ދައްޗެއް ނުވެއޭ. ޑޮލަރު އެބަ ލިބެއޭ، ބްލެކް މާކެޓުގައޭ ލިބެނީ. އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް؛ އާންމު ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތު މީހާއަށް އޭގެން ވަނީ ކޮން ފައިދާއެއްތޯ؟ ޑޮލަރު ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގައި ހުރެގެން އޭގެން އާންމު ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތު މީހާގެ ޖީބަށް ވަނީ ކޮން ފައިދާއެއްތޯ؟ އޭނާ ބޭރު ޤައުމަކަށް ބޭހަކަށް ޖެހިގެން، އެހެން ޒަރޫރީ ބޭނުމަކަށް ޖެހިގެންދާއިރު އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް، އޭނާއަށް އެ ވިދާޅުވާ ޑޮލަރުން ލިބެނީ ކޮން ފައިދާއެއްތޯ؟ އެ ވިދާޅުވާ ޑޮލަރު އޭނާއަށް ލިބޭތޯ؟ އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް؛ ނުލިބޭ. މި އުޅެނީ ޑޮލަރު ނުލިބިގެން. ވަރުވަރުން އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް، މި ސަރުކާރަށާ ނިސްބަތްވާ، މި ސަރުކާރުން އެކިއެކި މާލީ މަންފާތައް ލިބެމުން އަންނަ ވިޔަފާރިވެރިން އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް، ޓީ.ވީއަށް އަރުއްވައި ޑޮލަރު ލިބެއޭ ބުންޏަކަސް އޭގެ ޙަޤީޤަތް ބަދަލެއްނުވާނެ. އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް؛ ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުންނަށް އެބަ އެނގޭ ޑޮލަރު ނުލިބޭކަން. އަދި މިވާގޮތް ވެސް ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުންނަށް ވަރަށް ސާފް. އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް؛ މި އުޅެނީ ޑޮލަރު ނެތިގެން. ކީއްވެތޯ ޑޮލަރު ނެތީ؟ އިސްރާފު ބޮޑީ. އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް؛ އިސްރާފު ބޮޑީ. މި ސަރުކާރުގެ އިސްރާފު މާ ބޮޑީ. އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް؛ އެ ރަސްމާލެއެކޭ ކިޔާ ވެނިޓީ ޕްރޮޖެކްޓަކަށް ރައީސް މުޢިއްޒު ކިތައް މިލިއަން ޑޮލަރު ޚަރަދުކޮށްފިތޯ؟ ކިތައް މިލިއަން ޑޮލަރު ކަނޑަށް އަޅުއްވައިފިތޯ؟ އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް، ރައީސް މުޢިއްޒު. އޭގެން ކިތައް ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުންގެ ބޭސްފަރުވާގެ ކަންކަން ފުއްދުނީސްތޯ؟ ކިހާ ޑޮލަރެއް އޮތީސްތޯ؟ އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް؛ ހަޔަރ އެޑިއުކޭޝަންގެ ސްކޮލަރޝިޕްތަކުގެ ދަށުން އެތައް ޤައުމެއްގައި މިހާރު ކިޔަވަމުންދާ ކުދިންނަށް އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް، ސްޓައިޕެންޑް ޖަމާނުވޭ. ގަޑިންގަޑިއަށް ސްޓައިޕެންޑް ޖަމާނުވޭ. އެ ކުދިންނަށް މިނިސްޓްރީން ގުޅާފައި ބުނަނީ ތިމަންނާމެން
ކިޔަވަން އުޅުނު ދުވަސްވަރު އުޅުނީ އަދި ތިއަށް ވުރެ ހާލުގައޭ. އެއީ ޖަވާބަކީ އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް. އެ ހާލުގައި ނޫޅެންވެގެން ނޫންތޯ ވަރުވަރުން އިންތިޚާބީ މަގާމުތަކަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގައި މީހުން އިންތިޚާބު މި ކުރަނީ. އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް؛ އިންތިޚާބު މި ކުރަނީ ކޮންމެ 5 އަހަރަކުން އެއްފަހަރު އެ ހާލަތުގައި 80ގެ އަހަރުތަކުގައި، 70ގެ އަހަރުތަކުގައި ދިވެހިން އުޅުނު ގޮތަށް ނޫޅެން ނޫންތޯ. އެއީ މިއަދު މި ސަރުކާރުގެ ފަރާތުން އެކި ވުޒާރާތަކުން ވަރުވަރުން މަގާމުތަކާ ހަވާލުވެ ތިއްބެވި ބޭފުޅުންގެ ޖަވާބު އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް. މިއީ ލަދުވެތި ހާލަތެއް. މި ބިލާ މެދު އަޅުގަނޑުމެން މިއަދު ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ މި ރައްޔިތުންގެ މަޖިލީހުގައި، 20ވަނަ ރައްޔިތުންގެ މަޖިލީހުގައި ބަހުސްކުރަން ތިބެންޖެހޭކަމީ ވެސް ލަދުވެތި ހާލަތެއް އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް. މިއަދު ދިވެހިން ތިބީ ޑޮލަރަށް ޖެހިފަ. މިއަދު ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއަކު ޑޮލަރެއް ނުލިބޭ. 15.42އަށް ކީއްކުރަންތޯ 22އަށް ވެސް ޑޮލަރެއް ނުލިބޭ. އެއީ ޙަޤީޤަތަކީ. މި ޙަޤީޤަތް އޮޅުވައިލަން އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް، އަލްޓަރނޭޓް ރިއަލިޓީއެއްގައި ދިވެހިން ބައިތިއްބަން އުޅުނަކަސް މިއަދު ފަރެއްނުޖެހޭނެ. ފަރެއްނުޖެހޭނެ. އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް؛ މިހާރު އަނެއްކާ ވެސް ޑޮލަރުގެ އަގު ހުރިވަރު ކަމުނުގޮސްގެން އިތުރަށް މައްޗަށް ޖައްސާލައިގެން މި އުޅެނީ ފައިސާ ޗާޕުކުރަން އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް؛ ފައިސާ ޗާޕުކުރަން މި އުޅެނީ. ފައިސާ ޗާޕުކުރުމަށް ފަހު ޑޮލަރުގެ އަގު ދެން އަރާނެވަރު އަޅުގަނޑުމެންނަށް އަންދާޒާކޮށްލަން ވެސް ނޭނގެ. އަންދާޒާކޮށްލަން ވެސް ނޭނގެ. އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް؛ ޕެންޝަން އޮފީހަށް އައްޔަންކުރާ މީހާ އަނެއް ދުވަހު ހުންނަނީ އިސްތިއުފާދީފައި އެ އެއްޗެއްގައި ސޮއިނުކުރަން. ފައިސާ ޗާޕުކުރަން އެ ޖެހޭ ޑޮކިއުމަންޓުތަކުގައި ސޮއިނުކުރަން އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް، މުޅި ޕެންޝަން އޮފީސް އެއްކޮށް އެ އޮތީ ހުސްކޮށް. އެހެންނަމަވެސް، ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ މި ރައްޔިތުންގެ މަޖިލީހުގައި އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް، މިކަމާ ބަހެއް ބުނެލާނެ، ކަންބޮޑުވާނެ ސަރުކާރަށް ނިސްބަތްވާ ރައްޔިތުންގެ މަޖިލީހުގެ މެންބަރެއް ހުރިތަނެއް އަޅުގަނޑުމެންނަކަށް ނުފެނޭ. އަދިވެސް އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް، އަޅުގަނޑުމެންނަށް މި ފެންނަނީ ޙަޤީޤަތް ގަބޫލުނުކޮށް ޙަޤީޤަތް އޮޅުވައިލަން އުޅުއްވާތަން. އިއްޒަތްތެރި ރައީސް؛ ބާކީ އޮތީ 2 އަހަރު. ވަރަށް ބޮޑަށް ޝުކުރިއްޔާ.
speeches.en:
Thank you, Honourable Speaker. With the amendment the government has again submitted to the Foreign Exchange Act; Honourable Speaker, this amendment is in fact an admission that the government has failed. This amendment is an admission that the government's fiscal policy has failed. Honourable Speaker; it is an admission, Honourable Speaker, that the experiment President Muizzu has been conducting with the Maldivian economy until now, without the government understanding the financial situation, has failed. Honourable Speaker; about 2 years ago, the Maldives' Minister of Economic Development said very openly that if the PNC, the government, got a super majority in the People's Majlis of the Maldives, the price of the dollar would fall. Honourable Speaker; two years after that, the dollar that was then available for 18 rufiyaa is not available today even for 22 rufiyaa. Honourable Speaker; they say with great pride that there is no shortage of dollars. That dollars are available, that they are available on the black market. Honourable Speaker; what benefit does the ordinary Maldivian citizen get from that? What benefit goes into the ordinary Maldivian citizen's pocket from dollars being in the Maldives? When he has to go to a foreign country for medicine or for another essential need, Honourable Speaker, what benefit does he get from those dollars they speak of? Does he get those dollars? Honourable Speaker; no. The problem is that dollars are not available. Honourable Speaker, even if senior businesspeople affiliated with this government, who have been receiving various financial benefits from this government, are put on TV to say that dollars are available, Honourable Speaker, the reality will not change. Honourable Speaker; the Maldivian people know that dollars are not available. And what is happening is also very clear to the Maldivian people. Honourable Speaker; the problem is that there are no dollars. Why are there no dollars? Because the waste is great. Honourable Speaker; because the waste is great. This government's waste is far greater. Honourable Speaker; how many millions of dollars has President Muizzu spent on that vanity project called Rasmaale? How many millions of dollars has he thrown into the sea? Honourable Speaker, President Muizzu. How many Maldivians' medical needs could have been met with that? How many dollars would there have been? Honourable Speaker; the stipends of students now studying in many countries under higher education scholarships, Honourable Speaker, are not being deposited. Stipends are not deposited on time. The ministry calls those students and tells them that when we

were studying we lived in an even worse state than that. That is the answer, Honourable Speaker. Isn't it precisely so as not to live in that state that people in the Maldives elect people to senior elected offices? Honourable Speaker; isn't the reason elections are held once every 5 years so as not to live the way Maldivians lived in the 80s and the 70s? That is the answer today from people holding senior posts in various ministries on behalf of this government, Honourable Speaker. This is a shameful situation. That we have to sit debating this bill today in this People's Majlis of the Maldives, the 20th People's Majlis, is also a shameful situation, Honourable Speaker. Today Maldivians are desperate for dollars. Today no dollars are available in the Maldives. Forget 15.42; dollars are not available even for 22. That is the reality. Honourable Speaker, even if you try to obscure this reality and keep Maldivians in an alternate reality, it will not work today. It will not work. Honourable Speaker; now again, as the dollar price as it stands is not enough, they are pushing it up further in order to print money, Honourable Speaker; they are trying to print money. After printing money, we cannot even estimate how high the dollar price will rise. We cannot even estimate it. Honourable Speaker; the person appointed to the pension office resigns the next day so as not to sign that thing. So as not to sign the documents needed to print money, Honourable Speaker, the entire pension office has been emptied. However, in this People's Majlis of the Maldives, Honourable Speaker, we do not see a single member of the People's Majlis affiliated with the government who will say a word about this or be concerned. Still, Honourable Speaker, what we see is them refusing to accept reality and trying to obscure it. Honourable Speaker; 2 years remain. Thank you very much.

speeches.name: Abdul Raheem Abdulla
speeches.heading: ރިޔާސަތުން ވާހަކަދެއްކެވުން:

speeches.name: Abdul Raheem Abdulla
speeches.heading: ރިޔާސަތުން ވާހަކަދެއްކެވުން:
speeches.dv:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم މި ދަންފަޅީގެ މަސައްކަތް ފަށާނަން. މި ދަންފަޅީގައި އަޅުގަނޑު ނިންމައިލަމުން ވެސް ދަންނަވައިލި ގޮތަށް އޮންނާނީ ނިންމާލި އިރު ބަހުސްކުރަމުންދިޔަ ހޮޅުދޫ ދާއިރާގެ އިއްޒަތްތެރި މެންބަރު ޢަބްދުއްސައްތާރު މުޙައްމަދު ހުށަހަޅުއްވާފައިވާ ބޭރު ފައިސާއާ ބެހޭ ގާނޫނަށް އިޞްލާޙު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލުގެ ބަހުސް ކަމަށް އަޅުގަނޑު އޮންނާނީ ދަންނަވާފަ. މިހާހިސާބަށް މަސައްކަތް ފެށުނުއިރުގައި އެއްވެސް ބޭފުޅަކު ބަހުސްގައި ބައިވެރިވެވަޑައިގަންނަވާކަށް އެދިވަޑައިގެންފައެއް ނެތް. އެހެންވީމާ، އަޅުގަނޑު ގަސްތުކުރަނީ މިހާހިސާބުން މި ބިލުގެ ބަހުސް ނިންމައިލަން. ނިންމައިލުމަށް ފަހު ވޯޓަށް އަޅުގަނޑު ދާނީ. އެހެންވީމާ، ވޯޓު ރަނގަބީލު ޖައްސަވައިދެއްވުމަށް އިދާރީ މޭޒުގައި ދަންނަވަން.
(ވަގުތުކޮޅަކަށްފަހު)
# 9. ވޯޓަށް އެހުމަށްހުރި ކަންކަމަށް ވޯޓަށް އެހުން
speeches.en:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. I will begin the work of this session. As I said when closing, this session will be the debate on the bill to amend the Foreign Exchange Act submitted by the Honourable Member for Holhudhoo constituency, Abdul Sattar Mohamed, which was being debated when we closed. As of the start of work, no member has asked to take part in the debate. So I intend to conclude the debate on this bill at this point. After concluding it, I will go to the vote. So I ask the administration desk to ring the vote bell.

(After a short while)

9. Voting on matters to be put to a vote

speeches.name: Abdul Raheem Abdulla
speeches.heading: ރިޔާސަތުން ވާހަކަދެއްކެވުން:
speeches.dv:
ވޯޓަށް ދަންނަވައިލާނަން. ހުރިހާ އިއްޒަތްތެރި މެންބަރުން ވެސް ކާޑުކޮޅުތައް ޗެކްކޮށްލެއްވުމަށް ދަންނަވަން. މިއަދު މި އޮތީ ދެ ވޯޓެއް.
# {9.1}-
ފުރަތަމަ ވޯޓަށް މި ދަންނަވައިލަނީ ރައްޔިތުންގެ މަޖިލީހުގެ މި ހިނގާ ދެވަނަ ދައުރު 20 އޮގަސްޓު 2026ގެ ނިޔަލަށް އިތުރުކުރުމާ މެދު އިއްޒަތްތެރި މެންބަރުންނަށް ފެނިވަޑައިގަންނަވާ ގޮތަކަށް ވޯޓުދެއްވުން އެދެން.
[ވޯޓުދެއްވުން]
ވޯޓުގެ ނަތީޖާ:
| މަޖިލީހުގެ ޖުމްލަ މެންބަރުންގެ އަދަދު: | 93 |
| ހާޒިރުވެ ތިބި މެންބަރުންގެ އަދަދު: | 59 |

speeches.name: Abdul Raheem Abdulla
speeches.heading: ރިޔާސަތުން ވާހަކަދެއްކެވުން:
speeches.dv: ދެންމެ ނެގުނު ވޯޓުގެ ނަތީޖާ. މަޖިލީހުގެ ޖުމްލަ މެންބަރުންގެ އަދަދު؛ 93. ހާޒިރުވެ ތިބި މެންބަރުންގެ އަދަދު؛ 59. ފެންނަ ކަމަށް ވޯޓުދެއްވި މެންބަރުންގެ އަދަދު؛ 58. ނުފެންނަ ކަމަށް ވޯޓުދެއްވި މެންބަރަކު ނެތް. ވަކި ގޮތަކަށް ވޯޓުދޭން ބޭނުންނުވާ ކަމަށް ވޯޓުދެއްވި މެންބަރަކު ވެސް ނެތް. ވޯޓުގައި ބައިވެރިވި މެންބަރުންގެ އަދަދު؛ 58. ފާސްވުމަށް ބޭނުންވާ އަދަދު؛ 30. އެހެންކަމުން، ރައްޔިތުންގެ މަޖިލީހުގެ މި އަހަރުގެ ދެވަނަ ދައުރު 20 އޮގަސްޓު 2026ގެ ނިޔަލަށް އިތުރުކުރުމަށް ރައްޔިތުންގެ މަޖިލީހުން ފާސްވެއްޖެ.
speeches.en: The result of the vote just taken. Total number of members of the Majlis: 93. Number of members present: 59. Number of members who voted in favour: 58. No member voted against. No member voted not to take a position either. Number of members who took part in the vote: 58. Number needed to pass: 30. Therefore, the People's Majlis has passed extending this year's second session of the People's Majlis until 20 August 2026.

speeches.name: Abdul Raheem Abdulla
speeches.heading: ރިޔާސަތުން ވާހަކަދެއްކެވުން:
speeches.dv:
ސަރުކާރުގެ ފަރާތުން ހޮޅުދޫ ދާއިރާގެ އިއްޒަތްތެރި މެންބަރު ޢަބްދުއްސައްތާރު މުޙައްމަދު ހުށަހަޅުއްވާފައިވާ ގާނޫނު ނަންބަރު 32/2024 (ބޭރު ފައިސާއާ ބެހޭ ގާނޫނު)އަށް އިޞްލާޙު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލު ރައްޔިތުންގެ މަޖިލީހުން ބަލައިގަތުމާ މެދު އިއްޒަތްތެރި މެންބަރުންނަށް ފެނިވަޑައިގަންނަވާ ގޮތަކަށް ވޯޓުދެއްވުން އެދެން.
[ވޯޓުދެއްވުން]
ވޯޓުގެ ނަތީޖާ:
| ހުށަހެޅުއްވި މެންބަރު: | ހޮޅުދޫ ދާއިރާގެ މެންބަރު ޢަބްދުއްސައްތާރު މުޙައްމަދު. |
| މަޖިލީހުގެ ޖުމްލަ މެންބަރުންގެ އަދަދު: | 93 |
| ހާޒިރުވެ ތިބި މެންބަރުންގެ އަދަދު: | 59 |
| ފެންނަ ކަމަށް ވޯޓުދިން މެންބަރުންގެ އަދަދު: | 57 |
| ނުފެންނަ ކަމަށް ވޯޓުދިން މެންބަރުންގެ އަދަދު: | 00 |

| ވޯޓުގައި ބައިވެރިވި މެންބަރުންގެ އަދަދު: | 57 |

I ask honourable members to vote as they see fit on whether the People's Majlis should accept the bill to amend Law number 32/2024 (Foreign Exchange Act), submitted on behalf of the government by the Honourable Member for Holhudhoo constituency, Abdul Sattar Mohamed.

[Voting]

Number needed to pass: 29

Vote result: Passed

speeches.name: Abdul Raheem Abdulla
speeches.heading: ރިޔާސަތުން ވާހަކަދެއްކެވުން:
speeches.dv:
ދެންމެ ނެގުނު ވޯޓުގެ ނަތީޖާ. މަޖިލީހުގެ ޖުމްލަ މެންބަރުންގެ އަދަދު؛ 93. ހާޒިރުވެ ތިބި މެންބަރުންގެ އަދަދު؛ 59. ފެންނަ ކަމަށް ވޯޓުދެއްވި މެންބަރުންގެ އަދަދު؛ 57. ނުފެންނަ ކަމަށް ވޯޓުދެއްވި މެންބަރަކު ނެތް. ވަކި ގޮތަކަށް ވޯޓުދޭން ބޭނުންނުވާ ކަމަށް ވޯޓުދެއްވި މެންބަރަކު ވެސް ނެތް. ވޯޓުގައި ބައިވެރިވި މެންބަރުންގެ އަދަދު؛ 57. ފާސްވުމަށް ބޭނުންވާ އަދަދު؛ 29. އެހެންކަމުން، މި ބިލު ބަލައިގަތުމަށް ފާސްވެއްޖެ. ރައްޔިތުންގެ މަޖިލީހުގެ ގަވާއިދުގެ 106ވަނަ މާއްދާގެ (ރ)ގައިވާ ގޮތުގެ މަތީން މި ބިލު ދިރާސާކުރުމަށް މާލިއްޔަތު ކޮމިޓީއަށް ފޮނުވިއްޖެ ކަމުގައި ދަންނަވަން.
ނިންމުން
speeches.en:
The result of the vote just taken. Total number of members of the Majlis: 93. Number of members present: 59. Number of members who voted in favour: 57. No member voted against. No member voted not to take a position either. Number of members who took part in the vote: 57. Number needed to pass: 29. Therefore, this bill has been passed for acceptance. I announce that, in accordance with Article 106(d) of the Rules of Procedure of the People's Majlis, this bill has been sent to the Finance Committee for review.

Closing

speeches.name: Abdul Raheem Abdulla
speeches.heading: ރިޔާސަތުން ވާހަކަދެއްކެވުން:
speeches.dv:
ދެން މަޖިލީހުގެ ޖަލްސާއެއް އޮންނާނީ 13 އޮގަސްޓު 2026ވާ ބުރާސްފަތި ދުވަހު ހެނދުނު 9:00ގައި.
والحمد لله رب العالمين މަޖިލިސް ނިމުނީ.
speeches.en:
The next sitting of the Majlis will be held on Thursday, 13 August 2026, at 9:00 in the morning.

And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds. The Majlis is closed.
